method: Roi-Namur and Kwajalein are adjudicated separately from the 6-Feb dawn ground/sensor/AA state, then recombined through finite US gunfire/CVE/traffic and unloading wallets. No legacy D-Day casualty result is inherited.

US_first_day_ground_landing_KW.note: Killed+wounded+missing working combat/landing casualties through T24; the 5-Feb LST hit's 30-65 personnel effect remains separate. No KIA/WIA split is fabricated.

operational_result_T24.Roi: Organized resistance broken by late afternoon/early evening; isolated pockets remain.
operational_result_T24.Namur: US beachhead and most southern/central ground secure; coherent strongpoints remain in northern/eastern debris/vegetation belts. No island-secure declaration.
operational_result_T24.Kwajalein: Western beachhead secure and sustainable; armor/engineers/artillery ashore in useful mass and roughly western 40-50 percent of the island is controlled or dominated. Organized defense remains ahead of the beachhead.
operational_result_T24.D_day: Operationally successful but materially more costly and slower than the superseded v003 first-day line; no Tarawa-style landing failure.

Japan_combined_state_T24.northern_Roi_Namur: About 650-900 organized/local fighters remain centered on Namur plus roughly 350-500 scattered/support personnel capable of bounded local resistance; Roi has only small isolated groups.
Japan_combined_state_T24.southern_Kwajalein: About 1,900-2,300 organized/local fighters remain plus roughly 500-700 scattered/support personnel capable of local defense, carrying and observation tasks.
Japan_combined_state_T24.command: Island-wide control is badly fragmented; local phone/radio/runner nets and pre-registered sectors continue to generate resistance below fortress-wide command level.

guards: No Japanese tank unit is added to Kwajalein or Roi. Namur Type 94 remains 0-1 and is not an anti-M4 system.
Do not inherit historical or legacy ammunition-magazine catastrophe as a fixed event; Branch ammunition dispersion/blast separation changes the secondary-explosion risk.
Do not multiply casualties by a generic fortification factor; higher Japanese survivability is partly offset by stronger US preparation and faster local combined-arms adaptation.
Do not count the 5-Feb LST mission-kill as removal of a named tank/LVT company without cargo trace.
Do not count regional surviving aircraft as target-island runway strike aircraft.
next_frontier: 1944-02-06T24 Marshall local; resolve 6/7-Feb night infiltration/local counterattack and 7-Feb daylight reduction from this state.
